Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on January 28, 2025
Review Body:
This read like an eighth grade memoir with an author trying to impress her teacher. I had the text analyzed and was correct in my assessment. As someone who struggles with ADHD, I can understand how hard it is to tell a lifetime’s worth of information, but some of this was a mess.

My main issue with this book is that everyone else is to blame, and the author is always above reproach. When you are married to a billionaire, why do you care to describe yourself as a victim? We all have failures, but the author refuses to accept any part in hers.

It wasn’t the worst book I’ve read, but I wouldn’t tell anyone it was worth the three hours I spent reading it. Fortunately, I read this book for free from my local library. If you want to see what she thinks, get a library card and remember that we all have our own versions of history.

And, please note, I don't mean smut - I don't need to hear any gossip and trash talk - I would've just like a deeper look into her childhood, modeling career, and stint as First Lady.

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on January 17, 2025
Review Body:
Melania Trump's book is a summary of her life thus far. It is easy to see from her public persona that she is a private person with a cool, aloof manner. She tells us in this book so much more and yet so little.

Reading like an extended resume or curriculum vitae (CV), Melania gives us a very brief look at her childhood and family life. We are given only the facts that she wants us, and the media, to know. We can sense the girl who loves deeply, works devotedly, and creates passionately but this reader didn't feel any closer to the author. The book centers mostly around her time with her husband, from their first meeting to the present day. It is clear that she loves both her husband and her son dearly. But she is an independent woman who has a mind of her own and expresses her opinions boldly, even when at odds with her husband.

The writing is a bit stilted but flawless. The entire book is an affirmation of her love for her family and we learn little that is new about the Mistique of Melania.

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on January 15, 2025
Review Body:
Was so excited to get this book and gain insight on this incredible lady’s story. I was a little disappointed.

The book is extremely repetitive. Every other page she reiterates how excited and honored she is to have been First Lady; and how hard she worked. I don’t discount that. It just gets old hearing it so many times.

Was also a little put off by her descriptions of clothing. She has, obviously, had a life in fashion and that is important to her. But actually reading about some of the extravagance of her life didn’t exactly endear her to me. The chapter on her Be Best initiative was probably the best written of the entire book, and perhaps that is because here, finally, after so many pages we finally hear about something she is passionate about.

It was interesting to learn more about the role of the First Lady and I had no idea Melania’s actual accomplishments while in the White House.

In my opinion, the faults of this book lie mainly with the editor. No good editor would have allowed the repetitiveness. Whether it was entire sentences repeated, the same descriptive word repeated in the same paragraph, or the completely nonsensical chronological format of the book. The timeline was all over the place in spots and I found the word for word repetition of speeches that she or President Trump gave a cop-out. A good editor would have helped this book tremendously.

Overall an interesting read. But don’t bother buying it. Just check it out at your local library. Buy JD Vance’s Hillbilly Elegy instead.

Review Body:
Melania – Melania Trump – 2024 –
This NY Times bestseller highlights Melania Trump’s life of elegance, privilege, and prestige with over 150 stunning photographs from her personal collection. Typically, Melania wrote about herself on a serious superficial level: always conducting herself with “dignity and poise,” impeccable standards and ideals, valuing women’s independence and the right to choose, and mostly about her life pre-Trump, her lavish bridal-wedding prep, and redecorating the White House.

Melanija Knavs (1970-) was the second daughter born to working-class parents in Communist Yugoslavia, later called Slovenia. Highly intelligent and ambitious, Melania completed her education, and embarked on a successful international modeling career in Paris and Milian. After her arrival in Manhattan, she was introduced to Donald Trump (1999). Initially, their relationship remained discreet, as he was negotiating terms for a divorce settlement from his second wife, Marla Maples (m.1993-99). Melania and Donald Trump were married at the Church of Bethesda-By-The-Sea (Palm Beach, FL.) with an extravagant reception following at Mar-a Lago (2005).

Melania adores her husband and family; motherhood affected her in a profound way. Although Barron William Trump (2006-) is her only child, she attributes “good communication” as vital in her role as a step-mother to Don Jr., Ivanka, Eric, and Tiffiany. Reader’s will learn significantly more about Donald Trump’s individual style of parenting from Ivana Trump’s (1949-2022) memoir: “Raising Trump: Values from America’s First Mother” (2017).

There is nothing dignified about blaming mistakes, poor decisions, and missteps on the media or others. The jacket fiasco during the Texas migrant border crisis “I Really Don’t Care-Do You?” (2018) was not one of her best decisions. Melania’s Press Secretary resigned following the J-6 attack on the capital. Presidential historians and scholars will judge Melania for her lack of respect and consideration for Dr. Jill Biden; which was graciously extended (to Melania) by Michelle Obama during the peaceful transfer of power.
To her credit, Melania is a staunch supporter and advocate for children’s rights. The “Be Best Initiative” (2018-) combated student cyber bullying and the impact of the opioid epidemic in the lives of infants and children. “Fostering the Future” (2022-) is another signature program that awarded scholarships to students in foster care. As the first lady, Melania toured schools and children’s hospitals in Third World countries. 3* GOOD.

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on December 11, 2024
Review Body:
Writing aside, Melania offers great insight to the day-to-day of a First Lady, and inside the White House. Being about the life of Melania Trump, there is a lot of background on her upbringing as well - interesting, but the way it was included… I felt it could have been more of an overview for easier read instead of anecdotal like it was. Flow in a chronological format would have been helpful as well, but instead it seems like there were prompts being answered and the short answers were strong together to make a chapter.

Throughout the entire book, I could not help but find myself wondering if AI was used to construct the chapters. It seemed I would read a paragraph, and the next paragraph would have a rephrasing of the previous sentence somehow. Transitions were also lacking. Topic changes paragraph to paragraph did not flow and it seemed like the next was started with zero regard to the prior.

I did find myself highlighting some of Melania’s powerful words, and enjoyed seeing her perspective on many topics. I found myself surprised by some of the stances she has (in a good way) and also impressed by her depth. I would recommend this read in an abbreviated version as it could be much more concise and still have a good impact on the reader without losing details of Melania’s life or time as First Lady.

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on October 26, 2024
Review Body:
Writing a review will be hard, not because I don't have thoughts on it, but knowing/expecting that people will hate on it, as seen by the amount of hateful/negative reviews (many of which I suspect didn't even read the book, but just hate anyone/anything associated with the Trump name).

Anyway, having listened to a recent interview with Melania, I found the book reads much the same way as she speaks...meticulously...carefully choosing her words. I found some of her stories to be fascinating, and others to be meh. I like that she talked about the fact that she and her husband do not always agree on things politically. I think that is normal in most marriages, (at least amongst the people I know). I love how protective she is of her family and personal life, but especially her son.

It is not easy to live a life in the spotlight, and I would never try to put myself in her shoes or presume to know what goes on behind closed doors.

I enjoy reading biographies and getting a glimpse of their life. I do wish this book was able to humanize her a bit more. I feel like she held back a bit and would have liked more stories from her personal life. I was not aware that she was studying to become an architect when she started modeling, but understand now her love of design due to her mother's influence. I remember back in the day when she had a jewelry line out on QVC (back when the world loved her).

I feel that she has so much more she would like to say, but won't. To hear the things people say about her family, especially her husband, and stand tall, with her head held high, must be hard. I give her credit for that.

I enjoyed the book. It reads easy and is not overly long. The chapters are not long and drawn out.

I also had issues with the cover, looking like there were greasy fingerprints on it. Suspect it was partially because of the type of paper used on the cover.
